sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si* + *hubiera* + past participle, with *habría* + past participle, from B1 Unit 35. It describes a past that did not happen: *Si Sandino hubiera aceptado el pacto, no habría luchado en las montañas*. Both parts use *haber*: *hubiera* after *si*, *habría* in the result. Historians do this to explain why a choice mattered.

sections.title: The two parts
rows: Si Sandino hubiera aceptado el pacto, …
… no habría luchado en las montañas.
Si los soldados no hubieran salido, …
Never: Si habría aceptado el pacto…

items.spanish: Si Sandino hubiera aceptado el pacto de Tipitapa, no habría empezado su guerra en las montañas.
items.english: If Sandino had accepted the Tipitapa pact, he would not have begun his war in the mountains.

items.spanish: Si los campesinos no hubieran ayudado a los guerrilleros, la guerra habría sido más difícil.
items.english: If the peasants had not helped the guerrillas, the war would have been harder.

items.spanish: Si Sandino no hubiera ido a Managua, no lo habrían detenido esa noche.
items.english: If Sandino had not gone to Managua, they would not have arrested him that night.

items.spanish: Si el gobierno de Estados Unidos hubiera decidido quedarse, la guerra habría seguido.
items.english: If the United States government had decided to stay, the war would have continued.

sections.content: Use this form for what did not happen: it is a way to imagine, not a way to state facts. Never put *habría* after *si*: *Si hubiera aceptado*, not *Si habría aceptado*.
